name: Mapnik
role: C++ map renderer with Python bindings: geodata plus XML style to PNG
notes: 2026-11-27: Lead said Homebrew 4.3.2 and PyPI wheels; Homebrew install failed here (gdal conflicts with fbthrift) and conda-forge has no osx-arm64 mapnik. The PyPI wheel (4.3.2, cp312 macosx arm64, bundles libmapnik, plugins, PROJ, GDAL and DejaVu fonts) installs in a venv and was used. PyPI 4.4.0 (2026-11-25, Python >=3.11) is newer and untested.
2026-11-27: Python API differs from older docs: Image.to_string('png'), version_string(); mapnik.version is a function.

evidence.result: GeoJSON polygons, line and point label with XML style, 3 panned 512x512 frames; 7 probes exact in ImageMagick decode; alpha 255; shuffled equals sequential; two processes byte-identical; 1351 label black pixels; CPython 3.12, PyPI wheel
evidence.scope: PyPI wheel on macOS arm64, CPython 3.12: GeoJSON+XML style renders to PNG at predeclared pixels; bbox-pan frames deterministic. Not SVG/PDF/Cairo, PostGIS, projections or other fonts.

summary: Mapnik draws geodata (GeoJSON, shapefile, PostGIS) to PNG through XML styles on CPU; change the bbox per frame for a pan
use_when: Use to draw source geodata straight to raster maps on CPU, with no tiles, GPU or browser.
Use to render a camera pan as frames by changing the bounding box per frame.
avoid_when: Avoid when a MapLibre style or vector tiles are the input; use chiitiler or maplibre-native.
Avoid for simple geometry that an SVG drawn directly would express.

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install mapnik==4.3.2

assessment.rationale: LGPL-2.1-or-later (PyPI metadata and COPYING in the wheel), passes the free-software gate. The PyPI macOS arm64 wheel bundles the library, plugins and fonts, so no system install is needed, unlike Homebrew here. Differs from maplibre-native and chiitiler by drawing source geodata with XML styles instead of MapLibre styles. Text placement depends on the bundled fonts and version.
